title: Part 1: Where you live — simple vs better answers
sourceTitle: Most Common IELTS Speaking Part 1 Questions and Answers

segments.text: So, do you live in a house or an apartment?

First thing is connectors. Simple connectors like so, just connecting.

title: Part 1: A tricky question — can handwriting show personality?
sourceTitle: 8 Difficult IELTS Speaking Part 1 Questions (And How to Answer Them)
description: Cách trả lời câu hỏi Part 1 khó mà bạn chưa từng nghĩ tới: dùng "to some extent", "might give the impression", ví dụ thật — kèm câu trả lời mẫu.

segments.text: Do you think you can find out about someone's personality from their handwriting?
Low-level students found it difficult to understand the question.
Band 5 and 6 students would typically give me short answers, and band 7-plus students usually gave me an insightful answer with clever examples.
A useful approach when you get this type of abstract question is to think of a concrete example first.
For example, if the examiner asks, "Do you think you can find out about someone's personality from their handwriting?"
Picture someone whose handwriting you know.
Is it neat or messy?
Does that seem to match their personality?
Thinking about a real person or situation can help you form an opinion.
Now, let's look at some useful language.
If you're unsure, you can begin with it's hard to say.
For example, it's hard to say whether handwriting tells you much about someone's personality.
This acknowledges that there isn't an obvious answer.
Another useful phrase is to some extent.
This means something is partially true.
For example, to some extent, I think clothes affect my mood.
I tend to feel more confident when I'm wearing something smart.
You can also use might give you the impression that.
This describes what something could make you think without saying that your impression is correct.
For example, neat handwriting might give you the impression that someone is organized.
And a really useful phrase for questioning that connection is that doesn't necessarily mean.
For example, someone might have messy handwriting, but that doesn't necessarily mean they're a messy person.
In other words, one thing doesn't automatically tell you the other.
Finally, make your explanation more concrete with for instance.
You could say, "For instance, I feel more professional when I wear a shirt to work."
This gives the listener a specific example of the idea you're explaining.
Let's put it all together.
Do you think you can find out about someone's personality from their handwriting?
It's hard to say. Neat handwriting might give you the impression that someone is organized, but that doesn't necessarily mean they are.
For instance, my handwriting is quite messy, especially when I'm in a hurry, but I'm actually pretty organized in my everyday life.
Notice how the student acknowledges uncertainty with it's hard to say.

title: Part 1: Vocabulary to describe your home
sourceTitle: Essential Vocabulary for IELTS Speaking Part 1
description: Từ vựng tả nhà ở cho Part 1: well-organised, lots of natural light, overlooking the main street, close proximity to… kèm câu trả lời mẫu.

segments.text: I want to show you some vocabulary that students have used with me when I've been examining them that has impressed me immensely.

Another student described their home as being neat and tidy, a great collocation that means well organized.
Another student said their apartment was modern.
Another person said spacious, which means big.
Another person said light, which means there's lots of natural light coming into their apartment.
Now, here's a great phrase.
Once I was examining a student in Shanghai and they said, "I live in a typical Chinese apartment."
And then they explained what that is.
A typical Chinese apartment or you could say a typical Mongolian yurt or a typical Scottish tenement building.
This is a great phrase to use in your IELTS test when describing your home.
Perhaps your apartment is cramped.
It's very small. Learn some vocabulary to describe where you live.
Now, I want to show you some useful phrases as well.
You could say, "It has great views overlooking the main street."
Which means from your window, you can see the main street below.
What I like best is though.
What I like best is the proximity to the beach.
I live really close to the beach.
One thing I don't like is that my apartment is very cold in the winter.
I've been living here for 2 years.
I've been living here since I moved to Scotland.
So, we say living here for and then a duration or since and then a moment in time.
So, look at these sentences and make them true for you.
Do you live in a house or a flat?
I live in an old apartment on the outskirts of Edinburgh.
I've been living there for the last 2 years.
What's your favorite room in your apartment?
I'd say the living room.
It's a large room and I've got a massive and very comfy sofa.
Plus, a couple of weeks ago, I bought a projector, so it's great for getting cozy and watching movies.
Is there anything you would like to change about your home?
Interesting question. I wish my flat were better insulated.
It's fine in the summer, but in the winter, my flat gets incredibly cold.

title: Part 1: Give examples & compare past and present
sourceTitle: Give Better Answers in IELTS Speaking
description: Hai kỹ thuật kéo dài câu trả lời Part 1 tự nhiên: đưa ví dụ (for instance, such as…) và so sánh quá khứ – hiện tại (used to, would, these days…).

segments.text: Use words and phrases such as for example, for instance, such as, and like.
These are all ways that you can introduce examples.
You can say things like, "For my birthday, I like to spend time with small groups.
For example, just my close friends and family."
For instance, last year I invited my best friend and my sisters to play Settlers of Catan.
That's a board game, by the way.
My sisters are like me and love playing strategy games such as Risk or Settlers of Catan.
Although next year I want to try a board game I've never played before, like Distilled or Root.
Okay. So, by using these examples, you're showing the examiner that you can develop your answers.
Do you like eating sweet snacks?
I do. However, I try to only eat healthy snacks.
For example, I'll often eat protein bars or sugar-free brownies.
Do you like to travel to new places?
I do. However, I've noticed that I don't have as much interest in traveling to such far away places as I did when I was younger.
When I was in my early 20s, I really wanted to visit far-flung countries such as China, um, Japan, Australia.
Nowadays, I'm happier visiting the same countries over and over again.
The next technique is to compare the past and the present.
So you can use time phrases such as in the past something but these days something else.
I used to something however now something else.
I would something but nowadays something else.
When I was younger something but now something else.
Now you can use these time phrases interchangeably.
You can say things like, "In the past, I played lots of sports, but these days I'm not so into sports.
I prefer relaxing in my spare time."
Or, "I used to enjoy listening to techno music, but nowadays I prefer pop music."
When I was growing up, my family and I would visit my grandparents every summer,
but now they are dead, so I don't visit them.
By the way, would is a great way for talking about actions that happened repeatedly in the past.
And we often contract it.
So, we'd say something like, "When I was younger, I'd visit my grandparents every summer."

title: Part 2: Turn any topic into a story — the "but… so…" rule
sourceTitle: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Turn Any Topic Into a Story
description: Cựu giám khảo IELTS hướng dẫn kỹ thuật "but… so…" để biến bài Part 2 thành một câu chuyện, kèm bài nói mẫu "a special day which didn't cost much".

segments.text: I want to tell you a famous storytelling technique called the "but therefore" rule.
This was made famous by the creators of South Park.
Their idea is that if the events in a story are connected mainly by "and then" "and then" "and then" the story can start to feel like a boring list.
For example, listen to this.
I woke up and then I brushed my teeth and then I had a shower and then I went to work and I came back from work and then I had dinner and then I went to bed.
Boring, right? Instead, one event should lead to the next through "but" or "therefore".
"But" introduces a change, a problem or something unexpected.
"Therefore" shows the consequence, what happens because of it.
So I woke up but I realised my alarm hadn't gone off.
"Therefore" I was late for work and had to rush out the house without brushing my teeth.
When I got to work my new manager called me into his office but I hadn't brushed my teeth so while I was talking to him I kept trying to cover my mouth.
Do you see how this technique creates a much more interesting story?
Now, in natural spoken English we probably wouldn't keep saying "therefore".
We're much more likely to say "so".
As a result, for IELTS I want you to think "but so".
"But so". For example, we were planning to have a picnic but it started to rain so we had to find somewhere else to go.
Immediately we have a story because one event is affecting the next.
Here are some useful phrases for introducing the "but" part of your story.
"But then". But then just as we were about to start the picnic it began to rain.
The problem was. The problem was that none of us had checked the weather forecast.
Unfortunately. Unfortunately the rain got much heavier.
All of a sudden. All of a sudden everyone started running for cover.
To our surprise. To our surprise one of my friends came up with another idea.
And remember, what happened doesn't need to be dramatic.
You don't need to get lost in a forest or miss a flight every time you tell a story.
It just needs to change the situation and give you something else to talk about.
Let's continue our answer. I'd like to tell you about a really memorable birthday I had a few years ago.
At the time I was living in Edinburgh and didn't have much money to spend.
It was during the summer and I spent the day with a few of my closest friends.
We decided to keep things quite simple.
The plan was to have a picnic in the park so everyone brought some food and drinks from home.
We were hoping to spend most of the day outside and just enjoy each other's company.
But then just as we were about to start eating it began to rain.
Unfortunately it got much heavier very quickly so we all had to grab our things and run for cover.
That but gives us a turning point and the so gives us the consequence.
