title: What is there in your town?
sourceTitle: How to talk about your home town: Easy English Conversations Episode 3
description: Hỏi – đáp về thành phố của bạn: "What is there in Brighton?" — "There's a beach… There are lots of shops." Is there…? No, there isn't.

segments.text: Hello! Hi! How are you?
I'm good, thanks. How about you?
I'm very well, thank you.
Where do you live?
I live in Brighton.
What is there in Brighton?
Well, there's a beach, a university,
a train station
and a football stadium.
What else is there?
There's a cinema. Actually, no, there are two — three cinemas!
And there are lots of shops and restaurants.
There are some schools and gyms too.
Is there an airport in Brighton?
No, there isn't. Where are you from?
I'm from Petworth. What is there in Petworth?
Well, there's a school, a park and a market.
What else is there?
There are some restaurants and shops.
And there are lots of houses.
Is there a train station? No, there isn't.

title: What do you do every day?
sourceTitle: How to talk about your daily routine: Easy English Conversations Episode 4
description: Kể thói quen hằng ngày bằng thì hiện tại đơn: I wake up, I have a shower, I walk to work, I go to sleep.

segments.text: What do you do every day?
I wake up. I eat breakfast.
I have a shower.
I walk to work.
I listen to music.
I eat lunch. I go home and watch a film.
I eat dinner. Then, I read a book and go to sleep.
Georgie? Are you there?
Yep? What do you do every day?
I wake up. I have a shower.
I eat breakfast. I get the train to work.
I read the news on the train. I eat lunch.
After I finish work, I do some exercise.
I eat dinner. And then, I go to sleep.

title: How's the weather?
sourceTitle: Describing the weather where you are: Easy English Conversations Episode 8
description: Gọi điện cho bạn bè khắp thế giới: "Where are you? What are you doing? How's the weather?" — It's hot and sunny / raining / snowing.

segments.text: Hello, Buli! Where are you?
I'm in Mumbai. What are you doing in Mumbai?
I'm taking some photos.
How's the weather? Ooh, it's hot and sunny.
Where are you? I'm in London.
What are you doing in London?
I'm working. How's the weather?
It's raining. Hello! — Hi! — Hiya!
Where are you? I'm in Japan.
What are you doing?
I'm skiing. How's the weather?
It's snowing. Hello! Hi!
Hello! Hi. Where are you?
I'm in Beijing. What are you doing?
I'm shopping. How's the weather?
It's windy and cold.
Hello! — Hello! — Hi! Hello, where are you?
I'm in Argentina. What are you doing?
I'm eating lunch. How's the weather?
It's cloudy and cold.
How's the weather in Mumbai?
It's hot and sunny.
How's the weather in Japan?
It's snowing. How's the weather in London?
It's raining. How's the weather in Argentina?
It's cloudy and cold.
How's the weather in Beijing?
It's windy and cold.

title: How often do you…? Talking about habits
sourceTitle: Talk about your habits with Easy English Conversations Episode 12
description: Trạng từ tần suất: always, usually, often, sometimes, occasionally, hardly ever, never — Georgie và Tim kể thói quen của mình.

segments.text: Hi Georgie. Hello. What's your daily routine?
I usually get up at quarter to eight.
I often eat cereal for breakfast.
I always read the news on the train.
I sometimes exercise after work.
And I occasionally watch TV.
Do you sometimes go to the gym?
No. I hardly ever go to the gym.
Do you sometimes play video games?
No, I never play video games.
How about you, Tim?
What is your daily routine?
I sometimes get up at half past seven.
But sometimes, I get up at half past eight.
I occasionally eat toast for breakfast.
I always brush my teeth.
I usually walk to work.
I often read a book.
Do you sometimes go camping?
No. I hardly ever go camping.
Do you sometimes watch cartoons?
No, I never watch cartoons.

title: What did you do at the weekend?
sourceTitle: Talk about what you did last weekend: Easy English Conversations Episode 13
description: Kể về cuối tuần bằng thì quá khứ đơn: I went hiking, I made a cake, I had an ice cream — và Tim không được ăn bánh!

segments.text: Hi, Buli. Hi, Tim.
Where are you? I'm at work.
What did you do at the weekend?
Ah, the weekend. I went hiking.
Do you usually go hiking?
Yes, I often go hiking.
What else did you do?
I ate dinner with my friends.
What did you eat?
We ate pasta. I also watched a film at home.
What film did you watch?
I watched a horror film.
How was your weekend, Buli?
It was great. Thanks.
What did you do?
I went to the beach.
Do you usually go to the beach?
No, it's usually too cold.
What did you do at the beach?
I had an ice cream.
What flavour ice cream did you have?
I had a strawberry ice cream.
Sian? Are you there?
Yes I am. How was your weekend?
It was fun, thanks.
What did you do?
I made a cake.
What kind of cake did you make?
I made a chocolate cake.
Sounds delicious! Can I have some?
Sorry, Tim. My family ate it all.
What else did you do?
I went to the park and played frisbee.
Hello! Hi, Georgie. What did you do at the weekend?
I went swimming. Where did you go swimming?
I went swimming at the swimming pool.
What else did you do?
I read a book.
What book did you read?
I read a detective story.

title: Who's in your family?
sourceTitle: How to describe your family: Easy English Conversations Episode 15
description: Giới thiệu gia đình qua cây phả hệ: my parents, grandparents, aunt and uncle, niece and nephew, older/younger brother.

segments.text: Hi, Sian. Hi, Tim.
What are you looking at?
This is my family tree.
Wow! Who are they?
These are my daughters.
Do you have any sons?
No, I don't. Who is that?
That's my husband. And these are my parents.
This is my mum.
And this is my dad.
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
I have two younger brothers.
Who are they? These are my two nieces.
And this is my aunt, and this is my uncle.
Who's in your family, Tim?
This is my wife.
These are my parents: my mum and dad.
These are my grandparents: my grandma and grandpa.
And this is my aunt and uncle.
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
Yes, I have one older brother, and two sisters: One older sister and one younger sister.
Who are they? This is my niece and my nephew.

title: Clothes shopping: "Do you have this in a smaller size?"
sourceTitle: Talking about clothes shopping: Easy English Conversations Episode 19
description: Mua quần áo: How do these shoes look? They're a bit big. Do you have them in a smaller size / in black? I'll take them.

segments.text: I need to do some shopping too.
What do you need?
I need some shoes and some gloves.
How do these shoes look?
Hmm. They look a bit big.
Do they have them in a smaller size?
Excuse me. Yes. These shoes are a bit big.
Do you have them in a smaller size?
Yes, we do. How are these?
They are much better.
What else do you need?
I need some gloves.
How about these? How do these gloves look, Tim?
Have they got them in black?
Do you have these in black?
Yes, we do. They're much better.
I'll take them. What do you need, Georgie?
I need some trousers and some socks.
How do these trousers look?
They look a bit small.
Do they have them in a larger size?
I'll ask. Excuse me.
Yes? Do you have these in a larger size?
Yes, we do. How are these?
They're much better. I'll take them.
What else do you need?
I need some socks.
How are these? Do they have them in purple?
Do you have these in purple?
Yes we do. They're perfect.

title: What do I need in my new home?
sourceTitle: Describing your home: Easy English Conversations Episode 20
description: Georgie có nhà mới nhưng trống trơn! Từ vựng đồ đạc: bed, lamp, wardrobe, drawers, fridge, cupboards, oven, microwave.

segments.text: This is the bedroom.
What furniture do I need?
You need a bed.
A bed. You need a lamp.
A lamp. You need a bedside table.
A bedside table. And you need a wardrobe.
A wardrobe. Thanks. So, I've got a bed, a lamp, a table, and a wardrobe in my bedroom.
This is the dining room.
What furniture do I need here?
You need a table.
A table. You need four chairs.
Four chairs. And you need some drawers.
Drawers. Thanks! So, I've got a table, four chairs, and some drawers in my dining room.
This is the kitchen.
What do I need here?
You need a fridge.
A fridge. You need some cupboards.
Cupboards. You need an oven.
An oven. And you need a microwave.
A microwave. So, I've got a fridge, some cupboards, an oven, and a microwave in my kitchen.

title: What's your friend like?
sourceTitle: How to talk about personality in English! Easy English Conversations Episode 16
description: Tả tính cách: grumpy, brave, talkative, quiet, hardworking, lazy — và cách nói từ trái nghĩa "the opposite of…".

segments.text: Hi, Tim. Hello. Who's this?
This is my friend, Tom.
What's your friend like?
He's not friendly. He's quite grumpy.
He's usually angry or annoyed about something!
But I'm also brave.
I like extreme sports like bungee jumping, skydiving, and rock climbing.
Wow, that is brave.
Tom sounds like my friend, Gina!
What is Gina like?
She is sporty, and she is talkative.
Talkative. Tom isn't talkative.
He's the opposite of talkative.
He's quiet. He doesn't talk very much.
Sounds like Shannon! She's quiet.
She's also hardworking. Hardworking?
Tom isn't hardworking. He's the opposite of hardworking.
He's lazy. He sits on the sofa a lot and watches TV.

title: How do you take your coffee?
sourceTitle: How do you take your coffee? Real Easy English
description: Neil và Georgie trò chuyện về cà phê: take your coffee black/white, decaf, caffeine, cut down on — rất tự nhiên.

segments.text: So, Georgie, we're talking about coffee.
How much coffee, or how many coffees if we're talking about cups of coffee – how many do you have a day?
I usually have two, and I know that you do as well, because we drink them both in the office, don't we?
We have one cup of coffee in the morning and one usually in the afternoon, when we need to regain some energy and alertness.
Yeah. And so, we all know because we make each other...
at BBC Learning English, we make each other coffee, so we know how we take our coffee.
Yes. 'How we take our coffee' is how we like it – what we like to put in it.
For example, sugar or milk.
I know that you don't like milk in your coffee.
You take your coffee black.
I do. I like black coffee and you take your coffee white and you used to have sugar, but you don't anymore.
That's right. Occasionally when I'm at home I put some honey in my coffee to make it a bit sweeter.
Eurgh! Honey in coffee? Yes.
Is that surprising? I've never heard of that.
Really? Sugar, but not honey.
But why would that be so bad?
Well, I don't know. It's just I've never heard of it.
It's really good. I would recommend.
OK. So, Georgie, what happens if you don't have your coffee?
Well, in the morning if I don't have coffee, I feel very grumpy and very tired.
In the afternoon if I don't have a coffee, it's not terrible, but I would prefer to have my afternoon coffee.
How about you? Yeah, I need my coffee, especially in the morning, but I don't have my coffee first thing in the morning.
Oh, interesting. I have it, kind of, I don't know...
work time – nine o'clock. Why is that?
I think it's too strong, too powerful.
Or maybe just the way I drink it.
What happens if you drink too much coffee?
Ooh, then it's difficult to sleep because of the caffeine.
Caffeine is that chemical in coffee and tea that makes you feel awake and alert.
But too much means you're too alert.
I don't think that caffeine has a big effect on me.
I don't think I have trouble sleeping if I drink too much coffee.
It's strange. Yeah, because sometimes I'll have an espresso after dinner.
Really? Yeah. And I can still sleep.
That's crazy. Yeah. Lucky me.

title: Talking about lunch
sourceTitle: Talking about lunch: Real Easy English
description: Trưa nay ăn gì? leftovers, skip lunch, hangry (đói + cáu), brunch, working lunch, I'd rather…

segments.text: Hi, Neil. How are you?
I'm hungry. Me too. I'm starving.
Well, that's good, because we're talking about lunch today.
We're recording this just before lunch, so it's no wonder that we're both very hungry.
You might be able to hear our tummies rumble because we're hungry.
OK. So, shall we begin?
Yes. Let's do it. What have you got for lunch today?
Today for my lunch, I have chicken with potatoes and vegetables in a harissa paste.
Oh, that sounds really nice.
Yeah, it's leftovers actually, which I have heated up and brought in, in a little flask.
What are leftovers? Good question.
Leftovers. That's food from a meal that you've already had that you didn't finish and you can heat it up and eat it again.
Yes. I also have leftovers for my lunch today.
So, yesterday I made a pasta for lunch with vegetables in it and I have that.
So, Beth, what do you usually have for lunch?
Is it usually leftovers or something else?
It's usually leftovers when I come into work because it's easier, and then I don't need to buy lunch.
But if I go out and buy food, then I would usually go for something like sushi or ramen.
What about you? What do you usually have for lunch?
Yeah. Sometimes I have leftovers that I bring in.
Sometimes I buy a sandwich, for example.
What's your favourite kind of sandwich?
If I have a sandwich...
if I buy a sandwich for lunch, I like to get things like smoked salmon.
Nice, with pickles maybe. Yeah.
There's a really good baguette I like actually that has smoked salmon and egg mayonnaise in it.
Oh, it's so nice. Stop it.
Sorry. I'm so hungry. Me too.
Neil, do you ever skip lunch?
No. No way! I would be in a horrible mood if I skipped lunch.
I don't understand how anyone can skip any meal.
I need to eat all my meals.
Yeah. Otherwise, you get hangry.
Exactly. 'Hangry' is hungry and angry.
I'm on the... I'm almost getting hangry now.

title: Talking about restaurants
sourceTitle: Talking about restaurants: Real Easy English
description: Bạn có hay đi nhà hàng không? Gọi món, đặt bàn, nhà hàng yêu thích — hội thoại đời thường của Neil và Georgie.

segments.text: Hi, Georgie. How are you?
I'm great, thank you, Neil.
I just had a delicious lunch.
Oh, nice. What did you eat for lunch?
I had pasta. What did you eat?
I had a chicken sandwich.
Mmm. Well, today's episode is all about restaurants and food.
Great. I love it when we talk about food.
Me too. Neil, do you go to restaurants often?
Not that often. Maybe when I meet some friends.
How about you? Do you go to restaurants often?
No, I don't go often.
Probably once a month. OK, and when you go to a restaurant, what's your favourite part of eating there?
I like to be around lots of people.
I really love it when a restaurant has a good atmosphere.
I love spending time with friends.
What about you? Why do you like eating in a restaurant?
Well, I like to go to a restaurant that serves food that I don't know how to cook.
Yep, that's a good point.
So, restaurants with food from countries that I don’t know very well
or that are very different types of food to the food I make.
It’s really nice to eat out and that means to eat not at your home
because you don't have to make the food and you don't have to wash up.
That's true, yes. It’s also nice to eat out for a special occasion.
So, like a birthday or a celebration.
Yes and another special occasion could be something like Christmas and we at BBC Learning English are eating out for that special occasion.
We're having a celebration, aren't we?
Yes, every year we have a Christmas party and we usually eat out in a restaurant.
So, Neil, you said you like eating out in lots of different types of restaurants.
What do you usually order?
Well, I really like spicy food like Indian curries and I like fish.
So I like to get fish curry.
Mmm that sounds delicious! And we have a special way of ordering don't we?
What are some phrases we can use to order things in restaurants?
Yeah, so we can say: 'I'll have the fish curry.'
'I'll have the fish curry, please.'
Yes, and you can also say, 'Can I have the fish curry, please?', as well.

title: Talking about weekend plans
sourceTitle: Talking about weekend plans: Real Easy English
description: Cuối tuần này bạn định làm gì? Cách nói kế hoạch: I'm going to…, I'm planning to…, nothing special.

segments.text: How are you, Neil? I'm well, thank you, Georgie.
How are you? I am pretty good too, thank you.
I'm very excited for the weekend.
Oh, really? Well, today we're talking all about the weekend.
We're going to talk about what we plan to do at the weekend.
Great! Let's start. So, Georgie, do you have any weekend plans?
Yes, I do have plans.
I'm going to visit my parents at the weekend.
So I'm gonna get the train to my home town.
What about you? I don't really have any special plans, but I might spend lots of time doing sport with my kids.
Mm-hm, nice, which sports? Erm, cricket in the summer and football as well.
Nice. So that's what you usually do?
That's what I usually do.
I usually spend most of the weekend taking my kids to sport.
Do you like it? Actually, I really do.
I really do like it.
It's fun to watch them trying their hardest.
Ahh, nice. Is there anything else you'd like to do this weekend?
Well, I might meet up with a friend and we might go for some food
or maybe just a drink or we might go for a walk or something.
Mm, nice! And how about you, Georgie?
What do you plan to do when you get home?
Well, we have a lunch on Saturday.
And we live in the countryside, so we'll probably go for a walk with the dogs
and we're likely to go to the pub as well.
Mm. Is this a typical weekend for you?
It's not because I don't usually go home to see my parents.
Most weekends I stay in London.
I meet some friends. Yeah.
So this is not a typical weekend, but it's nice to visit my parents.
Mm. What are you looking forward to? — This weekend? — Yeah.
I'm really looking forward to spending time in the countryside.
When I'm in London, I really miss the peace and quiet.
And I miss my dog, so I'm looking forward to seeing my dog.
And it's good to get some fresh air.
Yes, exactly, exactly. So, Georgie, you said you are looking forward to being in the countryside.
I did. And 'looking forward to' means that you're 'excited about something you're going to do in the future'.
Exactly, yes. Like I'm looking forward to seeing my dog.
Is your dog looking forward to seeing you?
Yes, I'm sure he is.

title: Talking about public transport
sourceTitle: Talking about public transport: Real Easy English
description: Đi làm bằng gì? Tàu, xe buýt, đi bộ — chuyện trễ tàu, đông người và commute hằng ngày.

segments.text: Hi, Georgie. How are you?
I'm very well, thank you, Neil.
How are you? How was your journey into work?
My journey into work was very good today, actually.
And we're actually talking about transport today.
How was your journey to work?
My journey was quite easy this morning, actually.
It isn't always. And, Neil, we actually have a very similar commute, don't we?
I get the Tube to work, which in the UK is the underground train.
So, I walk to the station around 15 to 20 minutes, and then I get the underground train,
one train, and then I change and then get another one, and then I walk to work.
What about you? I do that, but before, before your bit, I have to get a bus as well.
Are you that far away from the station?
A couple of miles. OK.
Three kilometres. A bit too far to walk, then.
A bit too far to walk.
I have walked when the public transport has been unreliable.
But normally I... I get the bus to the Tube stop, and then I get on the Tube into work.
Lovely. And do you like the Tube?
What do you think about it?
I think the Tube is very convenient, actually, because the trains go very frequently.
So if you miss one, you can wait just a couple of minutes and get the next one.
And it's probably the quickest way to get into central London because there's so much traffic.
Driving is a really bad idea.
Yeah, I agree with you.
It is very reliable. It's usually very easy.
The thing I don't like about it, especially in the morning at rush hour, is the number of people on the Tube.
The... the underground trains in London are very old.
They're very small. And they are very crowded in the mornings.
So 'crowded' means there's lots of people.
We can also say 'packed'.
Yeah, and I really don't like being in a tight space with lots of people in the mornings, so early in the morning.
Yeah, I agree, but I'm lucky because I get on the Tube at the first stop,
so I always get a seat, but then by the time you get on, it is usually really packed.
And the closer you get into central London, the more packed it is.
You're squashed up against strangers.
It's not always fun. I hate it.

title: Talking about routines
sourceTitle: Talking about routines: Real Easy English
description: Một ngày của bạn thế nào? Buổi sáng, đi làm, buổi tối — từ vựng thói quen hằng ngày trong hội thoại thật.

segments.text: How are you today, Neil?
I'm very well, thank you, Beth.
How about you? I'm very good.
So what topic are we talking about in this episode?
OK, well, today's episode is all about habits and routines.
Now we talked about our favourite foods a few weeks ago.
But today we'll talk about our meal times and routines for eating.
Mm, sounds good! What do we mean by a routine, Beth?
Is it different to a habit?
Well, they are similar, but a habit is something we do regularly.
So, for example, I eat an apple and a banana most days. — Ooh, very healthy. — Yeah.
A routine, though, is slightly different.
It's usually more about the time that we do something and the way we do something.
So, I have my breakfast at 6am every day.
OK. You said you have your breakfast at 6am every day.
What do you usually have to eat?
Well, usually I have something simple.
A bowl of cereal, some toast with marmalade.
How about you, Beth? I usually have porridge.
And what about lunch? What time do you have lunch, usually?
Mm, I normally have lunch at about one o'clock.
What about you? Yeah, the same.
I don't like it at 12.
That's too early. But by two, I'm getting a little bit hungry and angry at the same time!
There's a word for that, Neil.
So if you're hungry and angry, we can combine them and say 'hangry'.
Yeah. So it's important to have regular meal times, so you don't get hangry.
That's true. Now you've just reminded me of another word which is 'brunch'.
Now, that's a combination of the words 'breakfast' and 'lunch'.
Do you ever have brunch, Neil?
I love brunch, especially at weekends.
Yeah. When I was at university, I used to have brunch pretty much every day.
So I would meet up with my friends and we would go to a café and we would have brunch.

title: Talking about pets
sourceTitle: Talking about pets: Real Easy English
description: Bạn thích chó hay mèo? Neil và Georgie kể về thú cưng — rất hợp cho Speaking Part 1 chủ đề animals/pets.

segments.text: Hi, Neil. How are things?
Very good, thank you. How are you, Georgie?
Yes, I'm pretty good, thank you, as well.
So, Neil, what are we talking about today?
We are talking about animals.
We'll be talking about pets.
OK, Neil. So do you have any pets?
No, I don't have any pets, but I know you do, Georgie.
Yes, I do. I have a black dog called Rafi. — Rafi? — Yeah.
Did you choose the name?
Partly, but it was a decision we made as a family.
Mm. Did you have pets as a child?
Yes, I did. We used to have cats, actually, we started with cats and then we got a dog and then we also had hamsters.
What about you, Neil? Did you have pets?
No, we didn't have pets when I was young.
Oh, I did have a goldfish called Gilbert.
But then, later on, when I was a teenager, my parents got a cat and a dog. — Wow. — Mm.
Did you have a good relationship with Gilbert?
I don't remember Gilbert, sadly.
But we had a cat that I liked very much and I've never really liked dogs, I'm afraid.
So, Neil, you don't have any pets now and you said you don't like dogs, but will you ever get one?
No, Georgie, I don't think so.
I will never get a dog.
That's OK. I mean, they're not for everyone.
What was your cat like?
The cat made me feel very calm, because she sat on my lap and purred.
You just used the word purr.
Can you explain what that is?
Yeah. 'Purring' is 'the noise that cats make'.
Not miaow. Miaow is... Purring is...
And the cat made that noise and made me feel calm.
Neil, that was a really good purr sound.
I would say it was purr-fect!
So, Georgie, what was your first dog like?
My first dog was really lovely.
I actually used to say that she was my best friend.
And we actually have a common expression to describe dogs, which is man's best friend.
'Man' here means 'human', so human's best friend.
That's because dogs are usually quite loyal.

title: Phrases natives use every day: "Well…"
sourceTitle: Phrases Native Speakers Use Everyday - Part 1
description: "Well…" — từ người bản xứ dùng mỗi ngày để có thời gian suy nghĩ và làm câu trả lời nhẹ nhàng hơn. Ví dụ vui: "Do you like my new dress?"

segments.text: Right, here we go. Number one, well.
Well. We use this for thinking time, but also sometimes to soften an answer.
Imagine the situation. Your wife, you're preparing to go out to a party.
Your wife puts on a new dress.
And she says, "Do you like my new dress?"
And you say, "Well, oh, I need thinking time.
What am I going to say?
Be honest? Be diplomatic? Yeah, it looks great.
And she says, "You don't like it, do you?"
You can't win. I know.
Or you might say, "Well, I'm not sure.
Maybe something more casual for this party?
So, here it's more about softening the answer.

title: Phrases natives use every day: "Actually…"
sourceTitle: Phrases Native Speakers Use Everyday! - Part 2
description: "Actually" để sửa lời người khác ("Actually, I live in Spain") hoặc thêm một sự thật bất ngờ — chú ý ngữ điệu xuống-lên.

segments.text: Number two. Actually. Actually. We use this for correcting people.
But also we use it to maybe add a surprising truth.
Correcting people. Imagine somebody says, "So Keith, you live in England, right?"
Actually, I live in Spain.
I'm correcting them. And often in this case we say actually, falling rising tone.
Actually, I live in Spain.
Okay. Keith, you don't eat fish, right?
